Inside the outlined area, all the way across to the bottom edge. Its top is about 4 1/2 in from the bottom edge.
Paint: Deep violet.
Brush: 1 inch flat.
Keep the brush level and the strokes long, left and right.
It should leave flat, level bands that seem to stretch away, with slight streaks that follow the stroke.
Watch out: Cutting the background in around each flower. Painting around flowers leaves messy halos and gaps. Fix: paint the whole field first, let it dry, then paint the flowers over it.

brushes.use: Lay in the deep violet field

steps.reason: cut from the finish inside the part's outline
steps.summary: Cover the whole bottom of the canvas with flat Deep violet for the lavender field.
steps.tip: Its top is about 7 1/4 in from the top edge, a level line straight across that butts up against the rolling fields and the bushes, and it covers the gold band at the bottom of the rolling fields, as the after picture shows. Run every stroke left and right, all the way to the left, right and bottom edges, so no white canvas shows.

lines.text: Let the lavender rows, and the far hills and fields dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Rinse the brush well first. Dirty water tints every color with the last one.
Inside the outlined area. Its bottom is at the bottom edge, and its left side is about 2 1/2 in from the left edge; it's about 11 1/2 in wide and 4 1/2 in tall.
Paint: Rust red.
Brush: 1/2 inch flat.
Mark one dot on the horizon. Draw three to five faint chalk or pencil lines fanning out from it. Pull each row's strokes along its line, wide in front and thin near the dot.
It should leave bands that narrow and bunch together toward one point, which is what makes the ground lie down and recede.
Leave what step 20 painted showing around these marks, as in the Result picture.
Watch out: Rows run parallel or cross each other. Fix: mark the dot and the fan of lines first. It takes a minute.

brushes.use: Pull in the rust soil between the rows

steps.reason: cut from the finish inside the part's outline
steps.summary: Pull rust red soil rows that fan out from one dot on the horizon.
steps.tip: Put the dot near the middle of the horizon: the middle rust row's middle is about 8 in from the left edge, and it's about 4 1/4 in tall, running from the bottom edge almost to the top of the lavender rows. The other rows fan out from the same dot, widest at the bottom edge and thin as a line near the top, with a few small rust flecks scattered between them as the after picture shows. Leave broad bands of Deep violet between the rows; the lavender goes there next.

lines.text: Let the lavender rows, and the far hills and fields dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Rinse the brush well first. Dirty water tints every color with the last one.
Inside the outlined area, all the way across to the bottom edge. Its top is about 4 1/2 in from the bottom edge.
Paint: Lavender purple.
Brush: #12 bright. Load: Creamy paint.
Stamp straight down with the end of the brush. Stamps side by side make a row.
It should leave a short, blunt block of color.
Leave what steps 20 and 21 painted showing around these marks, as in the Result picture.
Watch out: The same size and spacing everywhere. It reads as wallpaper, with no depth. Fix: smaller, tighter, and lighter at the back; bigger and wider-spaced in front.

brushes.use: Stamp the purple of the blooms

steps.reason: cut from the finish inside the part's outline
steps.summary: Stamp Lavender purple blooms along each row, following the soil lines.
steps.tip: Work back to front: small, tight stamps near the top of the lavender rows, bigger and looser ones toward the bottom edge. Follow each row along the Rust red soil lines toward the dot, and keep the Rust red paths clear. Leave Deep violet showing between the stamps and at the bottom of each row, as the after picture shows.

lines.text: Let the lavender rows, and the far hills and fields dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area, all the way across. Its top is about 4 1/2 in from the bottom edge and its bottom is about 3/4 in from the bottom edge.
Paint: Lilac.
Mix enough Lilac for this step and step 24; cover it between them.
Brush: #12 bright. Load: Creamy paint.
Stamp straight down with the end of the brush. Stamps side by side make a row.
It should leave a short, blunt block of color.
Leave what steps 20, 21 and 22 painted showing around these marks, as in the Result picture.
Lilac is much lighter than what it goes over: expect two or three thin coats, letting each dry.
Watch out: Covering all of the dark. The rows go flat, one value, with no depth. Fix: leave the dark showing at the bottom of each row and between the marks.

brushes.use: Stamp the lilac over the rows

steps.reason: cut from the finish inside the part's outline
steps.summary: Stamp Lilac on the tops of the lavender rows, leaving the darker purple below.
steps.tip: Keep the Lilac to the tops of the rows and the side of each row that faces the low sun; most of it goes in the top half of the lavender rows. Stamp it over the Lavender purple, not over the Rust red paths, and leave Lavender purple and Deep violet showing under each Lilac stamp.

lines.text: Let the lavender rows, and the far hills and fields dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area, all the way across to the bottom edge. Its top is about 4 1/2 in from the bottom edge.
Paint: Lilac.
Brush: #12 bright. Load: Creamy paint.
Stamp straight down with the end of the brush. Stamps side by side make a row.
It should leave a short, blunt block of color.
Leave what steps 20, 21, 22 and 23 painted showing around these marks, as in the Result picture.
Watch out: The light pass covered the dark. Fix: leave dark showing. Light over dark is what gives the row depth.
Step back, squint, or take a photo to see it whole, and compare the big shapes with the picture.

brushes.use: Tip the front rows with light

steps.reason: cut from the finish inside the part's outline
steps.summary: Dab bigger Lilac tips on the front rows near the bottom edge.
steps.tip: Most of this goes in the bottom half of the lavender rows, on the front rows nearest the bottom edge; the back rows stay as step 23 left them. Make these dabs bigger than the step 23 stamps and keep them on the tops of the rows and the side facing the sun. The change is small: compare closely with the after picture and stop before the front rows turn one flat light color.
paint_notes: Lilac is see-through over the dark purple: dab it twice where you want a bright tip, letting the first coat dry.
